newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates above 4 pct at month-end.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates above 4 pct at month-end.

text.p: German call money jumped to 4.25/50 percent on Monday amid a liquidity squeeze triggered by month-end obligations which banks had not fully completed last week, dealers said.
As banks scrambled to meet their requirements, rates pulled significantly higher from Friday's 3.00/3.10 percent rates.
But dealers also predicted that rates would normalise again fairly soon.
"Today we will not see any sort of decline in rates. But come Tuesday, rates could be back around 3.05/15 percent," a dealer said.
Dealers predicted that borrowings at the 4.50 percent Lombard rate would be quite high today.

Banks held 43.7 billion marks in reserve on Friday, down from the 44.6 billion marks held one day earlier. Meanwhile the monthly average stood at 40.9 billion marks after 40.5 billion marks one day earlier.

Lombard borrowings stood at 400 million marks on Friday, up from 100 million marks taken on Thursday. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 4.50000 percent on Monday after 3.07733 percent on Friday.
